doc.agent_version.description: The v2 agent build's own version, compiled in from the repo VERSION file at build time. Identifies which release produced this submission; unrelated to the instrument's own control-software version (see telemetry.instrument_control_version).

doc.product.description: The product bucket this build was compiled for (one build per product, FR-002b). Determines the watched-file set and which fleet token the binary carries. Only present in the heartbeat payload — the backup submission carries no product field of its own; its product is implied by the URL path.

doc.schema_version.description: On-disk format version of state.json itself (currently always 1). An unreadable file or a version other than 1 is treated as empty state (first-run semantics) rather than failing — this is a format tag for state.json, not a semantic version of the agent (see doc.agent_version).

identity.machine_id.description: Stable per-machine identifier: the Windows MachineGuid from HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Cryptography\MachineGuid, or the all-zero GUID if the registry key is unreadable. Distinguishes machines of the same instrument serial (e.g. after a reinstall) and machines that share no other identity.

identity.instrument_serial.description: The Luminosa/Solira instrument's own serial number, read from <data_dir>\Logs\LastOpenSerial.txt (last whitespace-separated token). The literal string "unknown" when unreadable (see identity.serial_source) — never omitted, so every submission is still attributable to a machine even without it. Not to be confused with the powermeter product's system_serial concept in the sibling pm100 app's dictionary, which identifies a different instrument being measured, not the one running the agent.

identity.serial_source.description: Where identity.instrument_serial came from this cycle: "file" (successfully read from LastOpenSerial.txt) or "unknown" (missing/unreadable). Lets a maintainer distinguish a genuinely-unknown instrument from a read failure without inspecting the machine.

telemetry.measurement_type.description: The generic PicoQuant telemetry endpoint's document-kind tag (shared backend machinery also used by other products, e.g. pm100's powermeter measurements use their own values of the same field). v2 heartbeats always send "agent_status"; the backup submission goes to a different endpoint entirely and has no measurement_type.

telemetry.channel.description: The build's compiled-in release channel (stable/beta). Never switchable at runtime. Reported so a maintainer can identify the beta cohort and spec 001's promotion gate can be evaluated from telemetry alone.

telemetry.os.description: Parent concept grouping the three OS-identification fields of the machine the agent runs on.

telemetry.os_build.description: Windows build number, as a string.

telemetry.os_arch.description: CPU architecture of the machine (not necessarily of the agent binary, though in practice v2 only ships x86_64).

telemetry.instrument_software.description: Parent concept for the two independent, individually-nullable readings of the Luminosa/Solira control-software version (FR-004a). Distinct from doc.agent_version, which is the v2 agent's own version.

telemetry.instrument_control_version.description: The version installed right now: the file-version resource of <install_dir>\<Product>.exe. Null if unreadable. Answers "what is installed", as opposed to telemetry.instrument_log_version's "what last actually ran".

telemetry.instrument_log_version.description: The version stamped in the 3rd ';'-delimited field of the header line of the newest *.pqlog under <data_dir>\Logs\ — the version that last actually ran (may lag telemetry.instrument_control_version after an install that hasn't been launched yet). Reading one header line is not log collection (FR-001 still holds; log contents are never sent). The exact header format is inferred from the current control-software build and not independently confirmed against a PicoQuant format spec.

telemetry.cycle_ok.description: True if the cycle completed without an *internal* error. A per-file block (locked/absent/too-large) or a backend rejection is an expected outcome and does NOT make this false — only FailureCategory::Internal on the heartbeat or on any file does (FR-002f). Identical computed value in the heartbeat payload (payload.cycle.ok) and in state.json (last_cycle.ok) — the same concept surfaced live and persisted.

telemetry.cycle_duration_ms.description: Wall-clock duration of the cycle that produced this heartbeat (backup pass + heartbeat pass).

telemetry.last_failure_category.description: The most recent *backup-submission* failure category recorded during this cycle's backup pass (ctx.last_failure_category), or null if none. This is NOT the heartbeat POST's own outcome — a heartbeat cannot report its own delivery failure inside itself, so this field only ever reflects a backup-pass failure from earlier in the same cycle.

telemetry.heartbeat_ok.description: Whether specifically the heartbeat POST of the most recent cycle succeeded — distinct from telemetry.cycle_ok, which is about internal errors across the whole cycle including the backup pass. Persisted only in state.json (last_cycle.heartbeat_ok); a heartbeat obviously cannot report its own success/failure inside its own body.

telemetry.blocked_backup.description: Parent concept for one entry of the heartbeat's blocked_backups list: a watched file that could not be backed up this cycle (FR-007).

telemetry.blocked_backup_reason.description: Why a watched file was blocked this cycle: "locked" (sharing violation), "absent" (file missing), "too_large" (over backup_max_bytes), or "rejected" (backend returned 422/400, FailureCategory::RejectedBadRequest). A narrower, file-outcome-only enum than telemetry.last_failure_category / FailureCategory — it has no authentication/backend_error/internal/no_network values, since only backup-pass per-file outcomes are surfaced here.

telemetry.cycle_counts.description: Parent concept for the per-outcome file counts of the most recent cycle, persisted in state.json for support/diagnostics.

telemetry.cycle_count_sent.description: Count of watched files whose action this cycle was Sent or Deduplicated (both count as a successful send, D-model FileAction).

telemetry.cycle_count_unchanged.description: Count of watched files whose action this cycle was Unchanged or SkippedToday.

telemetry.cycle_count_blocked.description: Count of watched files whose action this cycle was Blocked (see telemetry.blocked_backup_reason).

telemetry.cycle_count_retry_later.description: Count of watched files whose action this cycle was RetryLater (a transient failure — no state change, retried next cycle).

backup.file_key.description: Logical identifier of one watched configuration file, from the per-product WatchedFileSpec table (e.g. "pqdevice_db", "settings/DeviceConfig.xml"). Appears as a submitted field on the backup submission, as the map key of state.json's `files` object (the key itself carries this meaning, not a nested field), and inside a heartbeat's blocked_backups entries.

backup.content_hash.description: SHA-256 of a watched file's whole contents at the point it was read this cycle. Doubles as the wire integrity field the backend verifies/dedupes on (content_sha256) and as the on-device change-detection baseline (state.json's last_backup_sha256) — the same digest value in both places once a backup succeeds.

backup.gate_day.description: The UTC calendar day (YYYY-MM-DD) a watched file was last successfully backed up — the once-per-day gate's key (FR-011), evaluated in UTC regardless of machine local time. This is a DATE used to decide whether today's change may be sent, not a timestamp of when anything happened (that's time.cycle_started_utc) — a common misreading (FR-039). The same value is persisted per-file in state.json and surfaced read-only, per-file, in the heartbeat's last_backup_days map as a freshness hint.

backup.source_path.description: Absolute on-disk path the file's contents were read from this cycle (the real path/extension — v2 does not stage or rename files before sending, unlike v1's copy-to-.xml behavior).

backup.file_mtime.description: The watched file's own filesystem modification time at read time (optional — omitted if unavailable). Informational only; change detection uses backup.content_hash, never mtime alone (FR-010).

backup.content.description: The whole, self-consistent contents of one watched file at the point it was read this cycle (FR-015) — the multipart file part named "content". Never partial/torn; a file that changes mid-read is retried rather than sent inconsistent.

time.cycle_started_utc.description: The UTC instant this cycle began (captured once at cycle start, before any file reads or HTTP calls). Confirmed identical across every place it appears: the heartbeat envelope's measured_at, the heartbeat payload's cycle.started_utc, a backup submission's client_timestamp, a state.json file entry's last_success_utc, and state.json's last_cycle.started_utc all derive from the same captured value for a given cycle — not four different clocks, one clock read once.

time.cycle_finished_utc.description: The UTC instant the most recent cycle whose heartbeat POST succeeded finished (captured after the heartbeat pass, not at cycle start — deliberately distinct from time.cycle_started_utc). Persisted only in state.json's last_heartbeat_utc; not sent to the backend.
